Pursuant to Article 34 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2).

Under Article 23 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I request the registering of a First Information Report (FIR) and an investigation be initiated under Article 26(1) of the same Act.

Pursuant to Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek to adduce evidence of the occurrence, including the fact that the mobile phone was in my possession prior to its alleged theft and that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus.

## Summary
Based on the given context, you are seeking to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2). Your mobile phone was stolen from your pocket in a crowded bus.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 314]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given that the perpetrator(s) stole your mobile phone, which is a movable property, and considering the context of [BNS Section 314], it is likely that the perpetrator(s) have committed the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property'. I recommend that you file a complaint with the authorities, providing details of the incident, including the time, place, and circumstances of the theft. The authorities will then register a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 26(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 and initiate an investigation. As evidence, you can adduce details of your possession of the mobile phone prior to its theft and the fact that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus, which can be considered under Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Accordingly, a Bill, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 was introduced in the Lok Sabha 
on 11th August, 2023. The Bill was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs for its consideration and report. The Committee after deliberations made its 
recommendations in its report submitted on 10th November, 2023. The recommendations made by the 
Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

Petition for Investigation and Prosecution Pursuant to Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

It is respectfully submitted that on the night of [date], the respondent trespassed into the house of the petitioner at [address] by means of force (Article 17(1) of BNSS), wherein he committed the offence of misappropriation of the petitioner's personal property, specifically jewelry, in contravention of Article 201(1) of the BNS.

The petitioner humbly requests that an investigation be conducted under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence, and that the respondent be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Supporting documents and evidence are attached hereto.

Please accept this petition as a formal complaint.

Respectfully submitted,
[Petitioner's Name]
result.answer:
## Summary
The petitioner, a house owner, has been victimized by a trespasser who broke into their house at night and stole their jewelry. The petitioner has filed a petition for investigation and prosecution under Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 201] 
[BNS Section 4] 
[BNS Section 209] 
[BNS Section 199] 

## Recommendation / next steps
The Magistrate is respectfully requested to order an investigation under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence. The respondent should be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Additionally, the Magistrate may consider Section 199 of the BNS, which deals with public servants disobeying direction under law, in case the investigation reveals any discrepancies or omissions on the part of the public servants involved.

Further, in accordance with Section 209 of the BNS, the Magistrate may consider imposing community service as a punishment for the respondent, depending on the severity of the offence and the circumstances of the case.

Finally, the Magistrate is requested to ensure that the investigation and prosecution are conducted in a fair and impartial manner, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNS.

Your neighbor's statements threatening to cause bodily harm to you if you use the common parking area may constitute an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). In view of the potential for your neighbor's statements to constitute an offence under BNS, you may want to consider reporting these incidents to the authorities or seeking a restraining order to prevent further harassment. against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

[BNS Section 353] BNS_2023_s353 (Act: BNS_2023)
Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 
Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person 
making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as 
required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, 
or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Stalking.—(1) Any man who— 
(i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal 
interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or 
(ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic 
communication, 
commits the offence of stalking: 
Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man who pursued it proves that— 
(i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man accused of 
stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; 
(ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement imposed by any 
person under any law; or 
(iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified. 
(2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment

punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which 
may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

signs or by visible representations or through electronic means or otherwise, insults or attempts to insult 
the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description 
for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

Furthermore, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and Article 110, I request guidance on the necessary procedures and protocols to be followed to lodge a complaint, investigate the case, and ensure the apprehension and prosecution of the perpetrator, as well as compensation for the damages suffered by me.

Additionally, under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek to understand the admissibility and relevance of the forged cheque as evidence in the trial, specifically under Article 32, which deals with the Proof of Signature.

Lastly, I request an assessment of the liability of any financial institution or bank involved in the transaction, under the provisions of BNS and BNSS.

Query:

Pursuant to Article 34, Clause 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), has the landlord committed the offence of wrongful confinement or illegal detention under Article 42, Section 1 of BNS, by locking out the tenant from the rented premises without lawful notice, thereby rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings as mentioned under Article 19, Section 5 of BNS? 

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what procedures can be initiated under Chapter 3, Article 7, to secure the release of the tenant's belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws?
result.answer:
## Summary

The landlord has locked the tenant out of the rented room without any notice, rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings. This situation raises concerns about wrongful confinement and the tenant's rights under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 127] - Wrongful confinement
- [BNS Section 211] - Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the given scenario, it appears that the landlord's actions may constitute wrongful confinement under [BNS Section 127]. This is because the landlord has restrained the tenant in such a manner that prevents them from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits, i.e., the tenant is locked out of their room.

The tenant may be eligible for compensation for non-treatment under [BNS Section 200] if the landlord fails to provide access to their belongings. However, the tenant may need to take further action to secure their release, which could involve initiating procedures under Chapter 3, Article 7 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to secure the release of their belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws.

In the first instance, the tenant may want to consider reporting the incident to the local authorities, who can investigate the matter and take necessary action. The tenant may also want to consider seeking legal advice to explore their options for recovering their belongings and seeking compensation for any losses incurred.

Whether the alleged perpetrators of the incident, involving intentional damage to property (specifically, a commercial establishment), by means of hurling projectiles (stones) and causing intentional destruction of glass panes, have committed the offence of "Mischief" under Section 43(1) of the BNS? 

Additionally, I request an investigation into the circumstances surrounding this incident, as mandated by Section 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), with a view to determining whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the BNSS, which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the identification of the perpetrators and the reconstruction of the events surrounding the incident, in light of Article 17(2) of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of circumstantial evidence.

Given the facts of the case, it seems that the perpetrators may have committed the offence of mischief under Section 324 of the BNS. Therefore, it is recommended that the case be investigated further to determine the extent of the damage and the identities of the perpetrators.

Section 324 of the BNS provides for punishment for mischief, which may extend to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both, depending on the extent of the damage caused.

Additionally, since the incident occurred during a protest, it may be relevant to investigate whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

It would be best to consult with the relevant authorities and experts to determine the next steps and to ensure that the investigation is conducted in accordance with the provisions of the BNS and the BNSS.

Application of Section 306 of BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) for alleged offences under Section 506 of BNS, seeking redress under Section 155 of BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) for protection and investigation.

Whether the facts presented constitute a prima facie case of extortion under Section 306 of BNS, justifying the initiation of a police investigation under Section 155 of BNSS and whether the complainant is entitled to protection under the said Act.

Further, this application seeks clarification on the admissibility of electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, as per Article 59 of BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) for purposes of prosecution under Section 306 of BNS.
result.answer:
## Summary

The facts presented indicate that a stranger is threatening to burn the complainant's shop unless they pay money. This behavior constitutes a prima facie case of extortion under Section 308 of BNS, as the stranger is intentionally putting the complainant in fear of injury to their shop and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver money. The complainant is entitled to protection under Section 155 of BNSS for protection and investigation.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Section 308 (Extortion)
- Section 155 of BNSS (Protection and investigation)
- [BNS Section 5]

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the prima facie case of extortion, the complainant should file a complaint under Section 155 of BNSS for protection and investigation. The police should be informed about the electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, which can be used as admissible evidence under Article 59 of BSA. The complainant should also be advised to preserve any relevant evidence and to cooperate fully with the investigation.

A complaint has been filed against a neighbor who allegedly hit the complainant's brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument, leaving the brother in ICU and possibly facing life-threatening injuries. The complaint alleges offenses of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" (Section 306, BNS) and "Murder" (Section 307, BNS). An application has been made to register an FIR under Section 154, BNSS. The admissibility of evidence, including statements made by the injured party and medical evidence, is also being questioned.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 299]
- [BNS Section 302]
- [BNS Section 306]
- [BNS Section 307]
- [Section 154, BNSS]
- [BNS Section 59]
- [BNS Section 60]

## Recommendation / next steps

It appears that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) is the applicable law in this case. To proceed, the police should register an FIR under Section 154, BNSS and investigate the incident. The admissibility of evidence, including statements made by the injured party and medical evidence, should be determined in accordance with [BNS Section 59] and [BNS Section 60]. The complainant's brother's statement, if made before hospitalization, may be admissible under [BNS Section 59]. Medical evidence, including hospital records, may also be admissible under [BNS Section 60]. The investigation should focus on gathering evidence to establish the facts of the case and determine whether the alleged offenses of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" and "Murder" have been committed. The complainant should be consulted throughout the investigation to ensure that their rights are protected.

**INQUIRY INTO CIRCUMSTANCES SURROUNDING THE DEATH OF A FEMALE**

Pursuant to Section 176(1)(g) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a complaint is made against the husband and in-laws of the deceased for alleged commission of the offence under Section 312(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), read with Sections 312(2) and 312(3) thereof, arising out of the continuous harassment and torture inflicted upon the deceased by the accused.

The circumstances of the case, including the fact that the deceased was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage, necessitate an investigation to ascertain whether the death was caused by the accused's acts constituting the aforesaid offence.

The prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused under Section 101(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), which provides that the burden of proving the defence of the accused lies on them. Consequently, the accused must establish that their actions did not constitute the aforesaid offence or that they were not responsible for the death of the deceased.

The court is required to inquire into the circumstances surrounding the death and to determine whether the accused are guilty of the offence alleged against them, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNSS and the BNS.

A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death. Additionally, the necessary steps to be taken by the authorities under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically in relation to Article 167 (arrest) and Article 168 (custody), considering the life-convict's status of being on parole at the time of the incident.

[BNS Section 1], [BNS Section 109]

The life-convict's act of strangling another person to death would amount to an attempt to murder under the provisions of Section 109 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The authorities must also take into account the provisions of Article 167 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which deals with the arrest of a person. 4. **Article 17(2) of the BNSS:** Did the accused's actions constitute a breach of peace and public order, thereby warranting investigation under the provisions of the BNSS?

result.rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, what would be the penal consequences under Section 304A for the cook who, with the intention of causing harm, mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and caused the death of three guests?

Furthermore, under Article 22(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, would the cook be considered a "culpable homicide not amounting to murder" under Section 299, and if so, what would be the relevant provisions of Article 14(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 that would govern the investigation and prosecution of this case?

Additionally, under Article 15(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what would be the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with regards to the testimony of the cook and any other witnesses who may have observed the cook mixing the rat poison into the food, in light of Article 25(2) and Article 27(1) of the said Act?
result.answer:
## Summary
The cook intentionally mixed rat poison into the food served at a party, causing the death of three guests. This act is considered a criminal offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 304A]
[BNS Section 299]
[BNS Section 109]
[BNS Section 46]
[BNS Section 111]
[BNS Section 324]

## Recommendation / next steps
Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the BNS_2023, the cook can be punished under Section 304A for causing death by a negligent act. The cook's intention to cause harm and the subsequent death of three guests would be considered a culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 299.

Under Article 22(3) of the BNS_2023, the cook would be considered a culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The relevant provisions of Article 14(2) of the Bharati Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 would govern the investigation and prosecution of this case.

Under Article 15(1) of the Bharati Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the admissibility of evidence in this case would depend on the specific circumstances. The testimony of the cook and any other witnesses who may have observed the cook mixing the rat poison into the food would be admissible under Article 25(2) and Article 27(1) of the said Act.

The penalties for the cook would depend on the specific circumstances and the provisions of the BNS_2023. However, under Section 111, the cook could be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than five lakh rupees.

Petition under Article 12 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), seeking registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(1) of BNSS in relation to the alleged commission of the offence of Kidnapping for Ransom, punishable under Article 21 of BNS, and requesting immediate investigation and rescue of the child.

Specifically, the petition seeks to invoke the provisions of Section 2(3) of BNSS for the purpose of expeditious and fair investigation, and to obtain necessary assistance and cooperation from the authorities under Article 18 of BNS for the safe recovery of the child. 

Additionally, the petition requests the Court to direct the Investigating Officer to gather evidence and collect statements from witnesses under the provisions of Article 25 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and to submit a detailed report under Article 13 of BNS.

The petition also requests the Court to direct the Investigating Officer to gather evidence and collect statements from witnesses under the provisions of Article 25 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 137] Kidnapping
[BNS Section 139] Kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging

The Court should consider the petitioner's request and direct the Investigating Officer to register an FIR under Section 3(1) of BNSS in relation to the alleged commission of the offence of Kidnapping for Ransom. ## Summary

A young woman was lured with a fake job offer and trafficked to another state where she was forced into prostitution. A complaint has been lodged under Section 4(A)(i) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023) - 'Exploitation of Vulnerable Person through False Promise' read with Section 6(A)(iii) of the BNS_2023 - 'Conspiracy to Traffic Person for Commercial Sexual Exploitation'. The incident allegedly occurred as a result of an offence under Section 7(B)(ii) of the BNS_2023 - 'Forcing a Person into Commercial Sexual Exploitation'.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 4]
- [BNS Section 6]
- [BNS Section 7]
- [BNS Section 22] (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023)
- [BNS Section 28] (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023)
- [BNS Section 15] (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023)
- [BNS Section 19] (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023)

## Recommendation / next steps

It is recommended that a magisterial inquiry be conducted into the matter as per Section 22(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Necessary action should be taken under Section 28(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 to safeguard the rights of the victim. The concerned authorities should obtain and preserve evidence related to the offence, including any electronic communication, documents or other materials relevant to the case, as per Section 15(A)(i) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The victim should be examined as a witness under Section 19(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

Petition for the Enforcement of Protection of Personal Liberty and Prevention of Unlawful Restraint and Confinement under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Whether the actions of the auto-rickshaw driver, as described, constitute an offence punishable under Article 321 (1)(a) of the BNS (Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder) or Article 321 (1)(c) BNS (Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means) since these actions have not been specified and whether they fall under the provisions of Article 321(1)(h) of the BNS (Sexual Assault), or Article 321 (1)(j) of the BNS (Kidnapping or Abduction) and/or Article 321 (1)(g) of the BNS (Unlawful Restraint) of a woman passenger against her will.

Whether the police have a duty to register an FIR under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and to conduct a thorough investigation into this incident.

Whether the prosecution can rely on circumstantial evidence as per Article 59(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for conviction of the accused and the admissibility of digital evidence under Article 54 of the BSA.

Whether the accused can be held criminally liable under Article 21(7) of the BNS and the provision of anticipatory bail under Article 34 of the BNSS in light of these circumstances.
result.answer:
## Summary

The actions of the auto-rickshaw driver described in the query constitute a serious offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023). The driver's actions of forcibly taking a woman passenger to an isolated area against her will, without specifying the intent, fall under the provisions of Article 321 (1)(j) of the BNS (Kidnapping or Abduction) and/or Article 321 (1)(g) of the BNS (Unlawful Restraint). The BNS provisions also suggest that the accused may be held criminally liable under Article 21(7) of the BNS. 

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 1](BNS_2023_s1) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 4](BNS_2023_s4) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 113](BNS_2023_s113) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 125](BNS_2023_s125) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 200](BNS_2023_s200) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 211](BNS_2023_s211) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 209](BNS_2023_s209) (Act: BNS_2023)
- [BNS Section 113](BNS_2023_s113) (Act: BNS_2023) 

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the severity of the crime, it is essential to register an FIR under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and conduct a thorough investigation into the incident. The prosecution can rely on circumstantial evidence as per Article 59(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for conviction of the accused. The admissibility of digital evidence under Article 54 of the BSA should also be considered. In light of these circumstances, the accused may be eligible for anticipatory bail under Article 34 of the BNSS.

Pursuant to Article 12, Subsection 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek clarification on the applicability of Section 315A(1) of the BNS in relation to the alleged abduction of a minor child under ten years of age, in contravention of Article 316(2)(i) of the BNS, at a public gathering (mela). Furthermore, we seek guidance on whether the subsequent sale of the child to a couple in another city constitutes an offence under Section 318(2) of the BNS, thereby triggering the mandatory reporting requirements under Article 320(4) of the BNS, as amended by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Please note that the relevant evidence collected by the investigating authorities should be examined in light of the provisions of Article 41, Subsection 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically the burden of proof as per Article 42(3) of the BSA, to determine the culpability of the accused individuals.
result.answer:
## Summary

A child under ten was stolen from her parents at a mela and later found being sold to a couple in another city. The question is whether the alleged abduction of the minor child constitutes an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and whether the subsequent sale of the child triggers mandatory reporting requirements.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 139]
* [BNS Section 315A(1)]
* [BNS Section 316(2)(i)]
* [BNS Section 318(2)]
* [BNS Section 320(4)]

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the BNS provisions, the alleged abduction of the minor child constitutes an offence under Section 139, which deals with kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging. The subsequent sale of the child likely triggers mandatory reporting requirements under Article 320(4) of the BNS, as amended by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). The investigating authorities should examine the relevant evidence in light of the provisions of the BNS and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically the burden of proof as per Article 42(3) of the BSA, to determine the culpability of the accused individuals.

The factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions. This office seeks clarification on the applicability of Section 117(1) of BNS, relating to "Exploitation of Labour" and Article 10(3) of the BNS, which defines "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment". Additionally, guidance is sought on the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(1) of BNSS, in relation to the alleged contravention of Sections 23(2) and 24(1) of BNS, which deal with "False Promises" and "Confinement for Labour", respectively.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Section 117(1) relating to "Exploitation of Labour"
- Article 10(3) defining "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment"
- Section 23(2) dealing with "False Promises"
- Section 24(1) dealing with "Confinement for Labour"

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the information provided, it appears that the factory owner may have committed offenses under Sections 23(2) and 24(1) of BNS, which relate to "False Promises" and "Confinement for Labour", respectively. A complaint is being registered against the accused individuals for their involvement in the alleged commission of a cognizable offence under Section 3(1)(a) of BNS, read with Section 4(2)(i) of BNS, for engaging in human trafficking and forced prostitution.

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the provided context, it appears that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) does not have specific provisions for human trafficking and forced prostitution. However, Section 211 of BNS deals with the omission to give notice or information to a public servant, which could be applicable in cases of human trafficking and forced prostitution.

The investigating officer should be directed to collect evidence, including documentary and testimonial evidence, in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 13 of BSA, to establish the guilt of the accused and to bring them to justice.

It is also recommended to invoke the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to authorize the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) and to initiate an investigation under the supervision of a Magistrate, as per Article 50 of BNSS.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

[BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;

resource located in India.

if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita.

of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any

To Whom It May Concern,

Pursuant to Article 10(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I request clarification on the following incident:

A couple procured a 4-year-old boy from the caretaker of an orphanage, notwithstanding the caretaker's express lack of authority to transfer custody of the child. The circumstances raise concerns regarding potential contravention of Article 21(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and Section 8 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which pertains to the protection of vulnerable individuals, including minors.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence in the event that the caretaker asserts a colourable defence of ignorance regarding the illegality of the transaction.

Please provide your expert opinion on the applicable BNS and BNSS provisions, as well as the relevant BSA guidelines for assessing the validity of the couple's claim.

Yours faithfully,
[Your Name]
result.answer:
## Summary
The couple procured a 4-year-old boy from an orphanage caretaker without authority to transfer custody. The transaction raises concerns about potential contravention of Article 21(1)(c) and Section 8 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. The caretaker may assert a colourable defence of ignorance regarding the illegality of the transaction.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 4] - Short title, commencement and application
[BNS Section 139] - kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging
[BNS Section 137] - Kidnapping
[BNS Section 303] - Theft
[BNS Section 314] - Criminal breach of trust
[BNS Section 113] - Harbouring or concealing a fugitive or a person who has committed a terrorist act
[BNS Section 209] - Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the information provided, it appears that the couple may have committed a serious offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The caretaker's lack of authority to transfer custody of the child suggests that the couple may have kidnapped the child, which is punishable under Section 137 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

The couple's actions may also be considered as theft under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, as they obtained the child without the lawful guardian's consent. Additionally, if the couple intended to employ or use the child for begging, they may be liable under Section 139 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

A thorough investigation is necessary to determine whether the couple's actions constituted a terrorist act or harbouring/concealing a fugitive, punishable under Section 113 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The caretaker's defence of ignorance may be considered, but it is uncertain whether this would absolve the couple of their liability.

In any case, the couple's failure to appear at the specified place and time as required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, may be punishable under Section 209 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

It is recommended that a thorough investigation be conducted to determine the extent of the couple's liability under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

In light of the recent amendments to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I respectfully submit the following formal legal query:

Pursuant to Article 322(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I request investigation and prosecution of the aforementioned incident under the provisions governing theft and robbery. Specifically, I seek to invoke Article 154 of the BNS, which pertains to the offense of "dishonestly receiving stolen property", in conjunction with Article 156, which deals with the offense of "robbery".

I also request that the accused be charged under Article 378(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which concerns the offense of "assault or use of criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of duty", as one of the perpetrators allegedly displayed a knife during the commission of the offense.

Furthermore, I request that the prosecution take into account the provisions of Article 13(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, which deals with the admissibility of evidence, particularly with regards to the testimony of eyewitnesses, in order to gather evidence and build a strong case against the accused.

Finally, I request that the investigation be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 102(1), which outlines the procedure for registration of FIR and investigation of cognizable offenses.

## Summary
The incident involves three men on a motorcycle snatching a gold chain from the user while they were walking on the road, and one of them showed a knife. The user requests investigation and prosecution of the incident under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 154], [BNS Section 156], [BNS Section 303], [BNS Section 314], [BNS Section 111], [BNS Section 113]

## Recommendation / next steps
Pursuant to the user's request, the investigation should be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 102(1), which outlines the procedure for registration of FIR and investigation of cognizable offenses.

The accused should be charged under [BNS Section 154] for the offense of "dishonestly receiving stolen property", in conjunction with [BNS Section 156] for the offense of "robbery". The user's testimony about the incident, including the display of a knife, should be considered as evidence in building a strong case against the accused.

The provisions of [BNS Section 111] dealing with organized crime, and [BNS Section 113] dealing with terrorist acts, may also be relevant in this case, depending on the investigation's findings.

The prosecution should take into account the admissibility of evidence, particularly with regards to the testimony of eyewitnesses, in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Article 13(2).

Query: 
Pursuant to Article 43, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the actions of the seven armed men constitute the offence of "Dacoity" under Article 174, Clause 2, and if so, what are the relevant provisions of Article 43, Clause 1 for the determination of their liability, considering that they employed force or threat to gain entry and committed a breach of peaceful possession of the jeweller's shop, as per Article 43, Clause 2.

Additionally, under Article 56, Clause 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, whether the police have the authority to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant, given the circumstances of the breach of the peace and commission of dacoity, in accordance with Article 56, Clause 5.

Lastly, under Article 81, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the burden of proof that the prosecutor must establish to secure a conviction against the accused, and whether the testimony of the watchman, as a witness, will suffice to establish the chain of events, in accordance with Article 81, Clause 2.

## Summary
The seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash. This incident raises questions about the application of various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023). The first query concerns whether this constitutes the offence of "Dacoity" and the relevant provisions for determining liability. The second query pertains to the authority of the police to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant. The third query seeks to establish the burden of proof for securing a conviction against the accused.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 254]
- [BNS Section 148]

## Recommendation / next steps
To address the first query, under Article 43, Clause 1 of the BNS_2023, the actions of the seven armed men could be considered as "Dacoity" as per Article 174, Clause 2. The relevant provisions for determining their liability are those related to harbouring robbers or dacoits, as stipulated in [BNS Section 254]. This section imposes punishment on individuals who harbour or conceal robbers or dacoits, with the intention of facilitating their activities or screening them from punishment.

Regarding the second query, under Article 56, Clause 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the police have the authority to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant, given the circumstances of the breach of peace and commission of dacoity, in accordance with Article 56, Clause 5.

Lastly, under Article 81, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the burden of proof that the prosecutor must establish to secure a conviction against the accused is through the testimony of the watchman, as a witness, which will suffice to establish the chain of events, in accordance with Article 81, Clause 2.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147.—Whoever within or without and 
beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to 
overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State 
Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description 
which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. 
Explanation.—To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal 
omission shall take place in pursuance thereof.

The complainant has lodged a formal complaint against an individual who allegedly engaged in extortion and caused hurt to those who refused to comply with their demands. The complainant seeks to know if these acts constitute an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and the necessary steps for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR).

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 1]
* [BNS Section 3]
* [BNS Section 15]
* [BNS Section 199]
* [BNS Section 211]
* [BNS Section 353]

## Recommendation / next steps

The complainant should approach the local police station and submit a written complaint. The police will investigate the matter and record an FIR under Section 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. The complainant's statement and any other relevant evidence will be recorded, and the accused will be summoned for questioning.

If the investigation reveals that the accused has committed an offence, they will be charged under the relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The accused may be punished with imprisonment, fine, or community service, depending on the nature and severity of the offence.

The complainant should also be aware of the provisions of Section 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which deals with statements conducing to public mischief. If the accused has made any false statements or reports that have caused harm or fear to the public, they may be punished under this section.

It is essential for the complainant to cooperate with the police and provide any additional evidence or information that may be required to build a strong case against the accused.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as 
required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, 
or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Accordingly, a Bill, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 was introduced in the Lok Sabha 
on 11th August, 2023. The Bill was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs for its consideration and report. The Committee after deliberations made its 
recommendations in its report submitted on 10th November, 2023. The recommendations made by the 
Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

Public servant disobeying direction under law.—Whoever, being a public servant,— 
(a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the 
attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other 
matter; or 
(b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating 
the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation; or 
(c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 173 of the 
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in relation to cognizable offence punishable under

shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with

grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Petition for Registration of a Crime under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Investigation under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) - 

To Whom It May Concern,

I submit a complaint of dacoity (Article 321, BNS) that occurred on the night of [date], during which I was robbed of a substantial amount of cash and a debit card at gunpoint by two unidentified individuals near the ATM. The perpetrators restrained me against my will, thereby committing an act of physical restraint and confinement (Article 312, BNS).

I request that the relevant authorities under the BNSS immediately register a First Information Report (FIR) in this matter and initiate a detailed investigation. I request that the investigation proceedings be conducted in accordance with Articles 43 and 45 of the BNSS, which mandate the collection of evidence and the apprehension of the offenders.

I further request that the investigation be conducted under the supervision of the Magistrate (Article 91, BNSS) and that all necessary steps be taken to ensure my safety and well-being during the pendency of the investigation.

I request that the evidence collected during the investigation be examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Section 19 thereof, which deals with the admissibility of digital evidence.

I request that the investigation be concluded at the earliest and that the perpetrators be brought to justice.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

[Your Signature]
[Your Name]

## Summary

The complainant was robbed at gunpoint by two unidentified individuals near an ATM on the night of [date]. The perpetrators restrained the complainant against their will, thereby committing an act of physical restraint and confinement. The complainant requests that a First Information Report (FIR) be registered and a detailed investigation be conducted under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to apprehend the offenders.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 312] - Act of physical restraint and confinement
- [BNS Section 321] - Dacoity

## Recommendation / next steps

The BNSS authorities should immediately register a First Information Report (FIR) in this matter and initiate a detailed investigation in accordance with Articles 43 and 45 of the BNSS. The investigation proceedings should be conducted under the supervision of the Magistrate (Article 91, BNSS) and all necessary steps should be taken to ensure the complainant's safety and well-being during the pendency of the investigation. The evidence collected during the investigation should be examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA). The investigation should be concluded at the earliest and the perpetrators should be brought to justice.

omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India.

committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India.

(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;

resource located in India.

if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita.

Pursuant to Article 123 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that:

Whether the perpetrators of the armed robbery, who hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics, have committed the offense of "Dacoity" under Article 224 of BNS, which attracts the punishment under Article 227 of BNS?

Further, it is requested to examine the applicability of Article 235 of BNS, specifically the offense of "Criminal Intimidation" in this case.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedures to be followed in order to register an FIR (First Information Report) in this matter, and what are the steps to be taken by the law enforcement authorities under Article 12 of BNSS to initiate an investigation?

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with regards to the electronic devices stolen, and the statements made by the driver who was tied during the hijacking?

## Summary
The armed robbers hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics. This incident raises questions about whether the perpetrators have committed the offense of "Dacoity" under Article [BNS Section 224] of BNS, which attracts the punishment under Article [BNS Section 227] of BNS. Additionally, the applicability of Article [BNS Section 235] of BNS, specifically the offense of "Criminal Intimidation" needs to be examined in this case.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 309], [BNS Section 148], [BNS Section 231], [BNS Section 303], [BNS Section 254]

## Recommendation / next steps
The incident appears to be a clear case of robbery, which is punishable under Section [BNS Section 309] of BNS. The use of force, intimidation, and theft of electronics from the delivery truck suggest that the offense of robbery has been committed. Furthermore, the tying of the driver may be considered as causing wrongful restraint, which is an essential element of robbery.

The offense of dacoity under Article [BNS Section 224] of BNS may also be applicable in this case, as it involves the collective and organized act of robbery, which is not limited to a single individual. The punishment for dacoity is imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, with or without fine.

The offense of criminal intimidation under Article [BNS Section 235] of BNS may also be applicable, as the robbers used violence and intimidation to carry out the heist.

It is essential to register an FIR (First Information Report) under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and initiate an investigation under Article [BNS Section 12] of BNSS.

Regarding the admissibility of evidence, the electronic devices stolen and the statements made by the driver who was tied during the hijacking may be admissible as evidence in the case, subject to the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

I, the complainant, submit this petition, praying that an investigation be initiated under Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against my servant, who has committed the offence of theft by secretly making a duplicate key and using it to steal cash and gold ornaments from my almirah, in contravention of Article 174 (1) of the same Act.

The complainant's servant has committed theft by secretly making a duplicate key and using it to steal cash and gold ornaments from the complainant's almirah. [BNS Section 303]

Petition for Investigation and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

Whether the actions of the known criminal gang amount to the commission of offence(s) under Chapter III, "Offences Against Persons" and Chapter V, "Offences Against Property" of the BNS, specifically Article 12(1)(a) ("Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder") in conjunction with Article 13(2)(b) ("Voluntarily causing hurt") and Article 20(1)(a) ("Theft") and/or Article 25(1)(a) ("Dacoity").

Whether the said actions also amount to an obstruction of public service under Article 32(1)(b) of the BNSS, specifically Article 34(4)(a) ("Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant").

Pursuant to Article 41(3) of the BNSS, whether the investigating agency should initiate an inquiry and gather evidence in accordance with Chapter VII, "Investigation" of the BNSS, including the collection of physical evidence and witness statements.

Whether the collected evidence can be used as admissible evidence under Chapter IX, "Evidence" of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 23(2)(a) ("Relevant fact") and Article 31(1)(b) ("Motive, preparation, and knowledge").

## Summary

The known criminal gang's actions of stopping buses, beating passengers, and taking valuables amount to several offenses under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). These offenses include theft, dacoity, and causing hurt. Additionally, their actions may constitute an obstruction of public service. The investigating agency should initiate an inquiry and gather evidence in accordance with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). The collected evidence can be used as admissible evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
* [BNS Section 209] BNS_2023_s209 (Act: BNS_2023)
* [BNS Section 113] BNS_2023_s113 (Act: BNS_2023)
* [BNS Section 229] BNS_2023_s229 (Act: BNS_2023)
* [BNS Section 148] BNS_2023_s148 (Act: BNS_2023)
* [BNS Section 197] BNS_2023_s197 (Act: BNS_2023)

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the BNS provisions, the investigating agency should initiate an inquiry and gather evidence in accordance with Chapter VII of the BNSS. The collected evidence can be used as admissible evidence under Chapter IX of the BSA. The investigating agency should also consider charging the members of the known criminal gang under the relevant BNS provisions, including theft, dacoity, and causing hurt. The evidence collected should be used to prove the commission of these offenses and to establish the gang's involvement in the robberies.

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

Subsequent to receiving information regarding an alleged incident of misappropriation of company funds by an accountant, it is respectfully submitted that:

* The accused, in his capacity as an accountant, is suspected of having committed an offence under Article 123(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) by dishonestly misappropriating company funds.
* The accused allegedly created fake invoices and utilized them to facilitate the unauthorized transfer of company funds to his personal account, thereby causing loss to the company.
* We respectfully request that you initiate an inquiry under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to gather evidence and investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident.
* We pray that upon completion of the inquiry, you proceed to prosecute the accused under Article 123(1)(d) of the BNS and Article 28 of the BNSS, as applicable.
* We also request that you consider issuing summons to the accused under Article 20 of the BNSS to appear before the court and answer to the allegations leveled against him.
* We further request that you direct the accused to produce all relevant records and documents related to the company's financial transactions during the period in question.

Please find attached the supporting documents and evidence in relation to this matter.

Yours faithfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Designation]
[Your Address]
[Your Contact Information]

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Explanation 1.—A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding.

## Summary

The user has been a victim of a scam where the seller provided forged RC and insurance documents, and the car turned out to be stolen. The user seeks clarification on the applicable penal provisions, procedures for registering a complaint, and the admissibility of electronic records as evidence.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 209]
- [BNS Section 339]
- [BNS Section 113]

## Recommendation / next steps

Pursuant to Article 123(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the applicable penal provision for furnishing false documents appears to be [BNS Section 339], which deals with the possession of a forged document with the intention to use it as genuine. 

Regarding registering a complaint and initiating an investigation, according to Article 56 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the user should follow the procedures outlined in BNSS, which may include seizing the forged documents and the stolen vehicle as evidence.

As per Article 27(5) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), electronic records, including email communications and online transaction records, may be admissible as evidence in this case, including in relation to the seller's intent and knowledge of the vehicle's true ownership status.

Complaint under Section 414 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (theft by carrier) is warranted. 

It is submitted that an individual, purportedly a courier agent, did receive valuables for delivery with the intent to deliver them. However, the said individual has failed to deliver the valuables and has switched off his mobile phone, thereby making himself unavailable for communication.

Pursuant to Section 102 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the police may take cognizance of this offense and initiate an investigation.

As per Section 8 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the burden of proof to establish that the valuables were received by the courier agent for delivery and that he has failed to deliver them lies on the complainant.

A man called the victim's elderly mother pretending to be a bank officer and obtained her OTP, leading to the unauthorized withdrawal of Rs 2 lakh from her account. This act may fall under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 314] - criminal breach of trust
[BNS Section 209] - non-appearance in response to a proclamation
[BNS Section 211] - omission to give notice or information to public servant
[BNS Section 113] - definition of public functionary and terrorist act

Since the alleged offender impersonated a bank officer, it may be considered a form of impersonation or cheating. The BNS does not have a specific provision for impersonation, but it can be related to the concept of criminal breach of trust under [BNS Section 314]. This section deals with dishonestly disobeys the directions and employs the money in his own business.

To proceed, the victim should file a complaint with the police, and a First Information Report (FIR) should be registered under Article 154 (2) (a) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). The police will then investigate the matter, and the BNS provisions mentioned above may be applied.

The victim may also be eligible for compensation under Article 210 (4) BNSS. Additionally, the admissibility of electronic evidence, such as the OTP and transaction records, can be determined under Article 57 (3) (c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).
