Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is hereby submitted regarding an alleged contravention of Articles 321 to 323, punishable under Article 325 of the BNS, wherein a printing press within the vicinity of your residence is reportedly engaged in the fabrication of counterfeit currency notes, specifically the two-thousand rupee denomination, in contravention of the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

Notably, this incident appears to be in violation of the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which necessitates an investigation under the procedures established in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), particularly under Chapter VIII, Article 86, to determine the extent of the alleged offense and the persons involved.

In furtherance of this complaint, it is requested that the relevant authorities be directed to examine the evidence and apply the principles of proof as enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically under Article 17, to establish the guilt of the perpetrators and to bring them to justice.

## Summary

A complaint has been submitted to the police regarding an alleged contravention of Articles 321 to 323 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), punishable under Article 325 of the BNS. The complaint alleges that a printing press in the vicinity is engaged in the fabrication of counterfeit two-thousand rupee notes. The police are requested to examine the evidence and apply the principles of proof as enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically under Article 17, to establish the guilt of the perpetrators.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 113]
* [BNS Section 178]
* [BNS Section 1]

## Recommendation / next steps

A thorough investigation under the procedures established in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), particularly under Chapter VIII, Article 86, should be conducted to determine the extent of the alleged offense and the persons involved. The police should examine the evidence and apply the principles of proof as enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically under Article 17, to establish the guilt of the perpetrators. If found guilty, the perpetrators should be brought to justice and punished accordingly.

result.rephrased_query: Complainant requests legal intervention under Article 225 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for an alleged case of forgery, as the accused had allegedly offered and used counterfeit currency notes (five-hundred rupee denomination) to settle the payment for goods sold. Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

Pursuant to Article 420(1) BNS, I hereby submit a complaint against an individual for alleged commission of an offence of cheating and forgery, in contravention of Article 425 BNS, by creating a fictitious will in the name of my late father, thereby forging his signature and that of a witness, with intent to mislead and acquire property belonging to my late father.

**Request for Investigation and Relief under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

I request the authorities to register an FIR (First Information Report) under BNSS and investigate the said matter, as per the provisions of Article 154 BNSS. Further, I pray that the Court may grant me necessary relief and protection under Article 189 BNSS, as well as compensation for the loss and injury suffered by me due to the alleged forgery and cheating.

**Evidence and Inquiry under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA)**

In order to establish the facts of the case, I request the Court to summon the relevant documents and witnesses, as per the provisions of Article 34 BSA, including but not limited to, the forged will, the signatures of my late father and the witness, and any other evidence that may be relevant to the case. I also pray that the Court may direct the inquiry officer to conduct a thorough investigation, as per Article 41 BSA, and submit a report to the Court.

Based on the allegations, it appears that the individual has committed forgery and cheating, which are punishable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Section 209 deals with non-appearance in response to a proclamation, but it is not applicable here.

## Summary

The shopkeeper has been using fake stamp papers for executing property agreements. This act can be considered as forgery, which falls under the category of counterfeiting. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023) deals with various provisions related to forgery and counterfeiting. The potential liabilities of the shopkeeper include punishment for knowingly facilitating and/or participating in the execution of property agreements by way of forged stamp papers.

## Recommendation / next steps

The shopkeeper may face imprisonment, fine, or community service for knowingly facilitating and/or participating in the execution of property agreements by way of forged stamp papers. The corresponding provisions under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the prosecution and investigation of such offences may also be applicable. 

To proceed with the investigation, a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 may be issued, and if the shopkeeper fails to appear, he may be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service. 

Further, since forgery is involved, the shopkeeper may be charged under section 339 of BNS_2023, which deals with possession of a forged document with the intention to use it as genuine. The punishment for this offence may extend to seven years or even life imprisonment, depending on the type of document involved. 

A thorough investigation and prosecution under the relevant provisions of BNS_2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 will be necessary to determine the exact liabilities of the shopkeeper.

The employee in question has altered financial records in the company's accounting software to hide embezzlement. Additionally, the question seeks investigative measures under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and the admissibility of digital evidence under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

The investigating authority should gather evidence through digital forensics and preserve digital evidence. The digital records and evidence obtained may be admissible in evidence as digital evidence under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), subject to meeting the conditions and requirements for admissibility.

1. An offence under Article 123(1) of BNS has been committed, whereby a mob set fire to several houses, thereby causing damage to property.
2. The same mob committed an offence under Article 456(1) of BNS, wherein a member of the mob raped a woman whose family was fleeing from the mob, an act that constitutes an outrage of modesty and sexual assault.

Furthermore, it is requested to examine the applicability of Article 789 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the admissibility of the victim's statement as an exception to the general rule of hearsay evidence.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), an application is being made to invoke the powers of a Magistrate under Article 456(2) of BNSS to authorize the registration of an FIR and to initiate appropriate proceedings against the perpetrators of the offences committed.

A complaint is being filed for two alleged offenses: (i) arson by a mob, causing damage to property under Article 123(1) of BNS, and (ii) rape of a woman by a member of the mob, which constitutes an outrage of modesty and sexual assault under Article 456(1) of BNS. The victim's statement is to be examined as an exception to hearsay evidence under Article 789 of BSA, and an application is made to invoke the powers of a Magistrate under Article 456(2) of BNSS to register an FIR and initiate proceedings.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- Section 123(1)
- Section 456(1)
- Section 456(2)
- Section 5 (relevant to the enactment of BNS)
- Section 1 (relevant to the commencement and application of BNS)
- Section 209 (relevant to non-appearance in response to a proclamation)

## Recommendation / next steps
Pursuant to the complaint filed, the Magistrate is expected to examine the victim's statement under Article 789 of BSA as an exception to hearsay evidence. The Magistrate may also invoke their powers under Article 456(2) of BNSS to register an FIR and initiate proceedings against the perpetrators. The investigation and subsequent proceedings will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of BNS.

What constitutes the offence of 'terrorism' under the BNS, specifically in relation to the planting of an explosive device in a public place, resulting in the deaths of five individuals and grievous injuries to numerous others, in contravention of Article 15 of the BNS?

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedural steps to be taken by the law enforcement agencies in investigating and prosecuting such a heinous crime, particularly with regards to the collection and preservation of evidence (as per the principles enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, BSA)?

Whether the conduct of the doctor constitutes an offence under Article 32 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically an act of "Commercial Bribery" whereby a public servant demands or receives gratification other than legal fees for the performance of a service, as mandated under Article 32(1)(d) of the BNS 2023, in contravention of Article 32(2) thereof, which prescribes that no public servant shall accept or receive gratification for any service other than legal fees.

Furthermore, the doctor's actions may also be examined under Article 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which deals with "Neglect of Duty" by a public servant, to determine whether his refusal to treat the patient without payment amounts to a wilful neglect of his duty as a medical professional, thereby violating his obligations under Article 53(1) of the BNSS 2023.

Additionally, the admissibility of evidence in this matter may be governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Article 27(1), which deals with the admissibility of statements made by a person in the presence of, or in response to, a public servant, in this case, the doctor, in the course of their official duty.

## Summary
The doctor's conduct of demanding Rs 50,000 from a poor patient's family to perform an emergency surgery and refusing to treat without payment constitutes an offence under Article 32 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The doctor's actions may also be examined under Article 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for "Neglect of Duty" by a public servant. The admissibility of evidence in this matter may be governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 170], [BNS Section 200], [BNS Section 223]

## Recommendation / next steps
The doctor's conduct under Article 32 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 constitutes an offence of "Commercial Bribery" whereby a public servant demands or receives gratification other than legal fees for the performance of a service. The doctor's refusal to treat the patient without payment also constitutes a "Neglect of Duty" under Article 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. The admissibility of evidence in this matter is governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. The doctor should be punished under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which include imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

Pursuant to Article 3(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek clarification on the applicability of the provisions governing 'assault' and 'outraging of modesty of a person', as defined in Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body', and Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty', respectively, to the factual scenario wherein a group of men physically attacked and verbally abused a Dalit family in an act that appears to be motivated by casteism.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy', we inquire about the potential applicability of this provision to the group of perpetrators, considering the concerted and premeditated nature of their actions.

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses', we seek guidance on the procedures to be followed in registering and investigating this incident, as well as the measures that can be taken to safeguard the Dalit family's rights and interests.

Finally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), Chapter VII, Section 7, 'Relevant and Admissible Evidence', we request clarification on the admissibility of the casteist slurs uttered by the perpetrators as evidence of their intent and the potential for these to be considered as aggravating factors in the trial.

## Summary

In the given scenario, a group of men forcibly entered a Dalit family's home, beat them severely, destroyed their household items, and hurled casteist slurs at them. This incident appears to be motivated by casteism. The perpetrators' actions can be analyzed under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body'
- Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty'
- Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy'
- Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses' (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023)
- Chapter VII, Section 7, 'Relevant and Admissible Evidence' (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023)

## Recommendation / next steps

The perpetrators can be charged under the provisions of Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body' for assault, and Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty' for outraging the modesty of the Dalit family members. Considering the concerted and premeditated nature of their actions, they may also be charged under Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy'.

For the registration and investigation of this incident, the procedures to be followed can be found in Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses' of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. Measures to safeguard the Dalit family's rights and interests should be taken according to this provision.

Regarding the admissibility of the casteist slurs as evidence of intent, they may be considered under Chapter VII, Section 7, 'Relevant and Admissible Evidence' of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. These slurs can be used as aggravating factors in the trial.

As the perpetrators' actions were motivated by casteism, they may also be charged under Section 196, 'Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony.'

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

[BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

[BNS Section 209] BNS_2023_s209 (Act: BNS_2023)
Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as 
required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, 
or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

[BNS Section 197] BNS_2023_s197 (Act: BNS_2023)
Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.—(1) Whoever, by words either 
spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic communication or 
otherwise,— 
(a) makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being 
members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith 
and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and 
integrity of India; or

(b) asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons shall, by reason of 
their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, be 
denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India; or 
(c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any 
class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional 
group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause 
disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons; or 
(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
